Croatian National Theatre

The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Square

    Ban Jelačić Square

    Anton Dominik Fernkorn’s statue was put up in 1866, removed by the communist authorities in 1947 and returned in 1990. Locals simply call the square Jelačić plac and meet under the clock.

    Look for

    The Manduševac fountain sits low in the paving. Legend says the city’s name comes from a ban asking a girl, Manda, to scoop up water for him.

  2. 02
    Culture · 1895

    Croatian National Theatre

    The Viennese architects Fellner & Helmer designed it, and Emperor Franz Joseph attended its opening in 1895. Opera, ballet and drama are still staged here.

    Look for

    In front of the theatre, Ivan Meštrović’s Well of Life shows naked figures twisting around a sunken basin.

  3. 03
    Market · 1930

    Dolac Market

    It opened in 1930 on the site of older houses cleared to make room. The red umbrellas echo the traditional umbrellas of the village of Šestine.

    Look for

    By the market steps, a bronze kumica, a peasant woman with a basket on her head, stands for the women who brought produce in from the villages.

  4. 04
    Viewpoint

    Lotrščak Tower

    The tower was built in the 13th century to guard the southern gate of Gradec. Since 1877 a cannon has been fired from it every day at noon.

    Look for

    Just below the tower, the funicular climbs from the Lower Town. Its track is only 66 metres long.

  5. 05
    Landmark · 1876

    Mirogoj Cemetery

    It opened in 1876, and Hermann Bollé designed its arcades. Catholics, Orthodox, Protestants, Jews and Muslims are buried side by side, and Croatia’s first president Franjo Tuđman lies here.

    Look for

    Among the graves, the basketball player Dražen Petrović’s memorial is still visited and left with flowers.

  6. 06
    Church

    St. Mark’s Church

    The church dates back to the 13th century and was restored by Hermann Bollé in the late 19th century. The patterned roof tiles date from that restoration.

    Look for

    The Gothic south portal is crowded with stone figures of saints and apostles, Mary and the Christ Child among them.

  7. 07
    Landmark

    Stone Gate

    It is the last of the medieval town gates of Gradec. A painting of Mary kept here survived the great fire of 1731, and people have come to pray at it ever since.

    Look for

    The walls are covered with small stone plaques saying thank you, hvala, left by people whose prayers were answered.

  8. 08
    Neighbourhood

    Upper Town

    King Béla IV made Gradec a free royal town in 1242 after the Mongol invasion. Its gas lamps are still lit by hand every evening.

    Look for

    On the Strossmayer promenade, the poet Antun Gustav Matoš sits on a bronze bench, looking over the Lower Town.

  9. 09
    Church

    Zagreb Cathedral

    After the earthquake of 1880 it was rebuilt by Hermann Bollé, who gave it its twin spires. The 2020 earthquake broke off the top of one of them.

    Look for

    Inside on the north wall, a clock face is stopped at 7:03, the moment the earthquake struck in 1880.
